## Vehicle, Animal etc.


Configuration Management Database (CMDB)
A database used to store configuration records throughout their Lifecycle. The Configuration Management System maintains one or more CMDBs, and each CMDB
stores attributes of CIs, and Relationships with other CIs.
Base Table
The core Configuration Item [cmdb_ci] table, which stores the basic attributes of all the CIs. All configuration item classes extend from this table including all hardware and
applications.
CI Reclassification Is a CI whose class has been upgraded, downgraded, or switched. An example of an
upgraded CI is a Server record that was upgraded from the Server [cmdb_ci_server] class to the Windows Server [cmdb_ci_win_server] class.
Parent and Child Class A table that extends another table is called a child class, and the table it extends is the parent class. A table can be both a parent and child class both extending and providing extensions for other tables. For example, the Server table extends the Computer table and the Windows Server table extends the Server table, thus making the Server table both a Parent and Child class.
Asset vs. CI On the Now platform, when creating a hardware asset, a corresponding CI will be automatically created or when a CI is discovered for the first time and inserted into the CMDB, a corresponding asset record will be automatically created. The asset and the CI is connected through out the CI/Asset lifecycle.

## Limiting Discovery Data:  Improves data accuracy



- o Avoids populating the CMDB with low-priority or irrelevant data.


  - Establishes a strong foundation with high-quality CIs.
- Prevents CMDB data overload
  - Reduces clutter caused by unnecessary Discovery results. o Keeps the CMDB clean and maintainable.
- Faster initial deployment
  - →Fewer devices scanned quicker Discovery cycles. o Enables a usable CMDB early, with gradual expansion later.
- Simplifies CMDB management
  - Focuses on key CI classes (e.g., servers, critical applications). o Ensures data is immediately relevant to business needs.
- Better stakeholder buy-in
  - Quick wins with accurate data build trust. o Encourages support for broader Discovery adoption later.
- ✔ Key takeaway: Start small, discover what matters first, then expand Discovery incrementally.
Discovery Ranges: Discovery ranges define which IP addresses ServiceNow Discovery scans.  You can include or exclude specific IP ranges in a Discovery schedule.  Broad Ranges (Subnets)
- Example:
  - 192.168.0.0/24 o 10.11.128.192/26
- Includes network and broadcast addresses.  Scans a large number of IPs, which may cause:
  - Data overload o Redundant or irrelevant CIs o Discovery errors
- Not recommended during initial implementation.  Best practice: Do not exceed /16 (~65,000 IPs); split into smaller ranges if needed.

- Imports data from files, databases, or APIs into staging tables.  Supports field mapping and transform scripts.

reconciles CI data from multiple sources, including manual imports.
- Identification rules are defined per CI class and consist of identifier entries
(unique attribute sets with priorities) and related entries.
- By default, IRE is not used during imports. It must be explicitly enabled using a custom onBefore script in the transform map.  The CMDBTransformUtil API sends import set data to the IRE for identification
before insert/update.
- IRE determines whether a CI is new or existing:
  - →New CI Insert into CMDB o Existing CI → Update the existing record
- When using CMDBTransformUtil, coalesce settings are ignored and are not
required.
Data Manager Data Manager enables periodic certification and auditing of CMDB data to ensure
accuracy and completeness.
- It uses scheduled certification policies that assign verification tasks to responsible
users or groups.

to all CIs in the class not linked to a Technology Management Offering.

Key Points  No base system orphan rules exist by default.  Orphan tracking requires custom orphan rules.  Only one orphan rule per class is allowed. - VM with no relationship to an ESX host  Hardware CI with no owner  Tomcat app with no relationship to a WAR file

## Reconciliation Rule How to Prevent Inserts?


Reconciliation rules help prevent updates from unauthorized or unwanted sources or
lower-priority sources from overwriting data provided by higher-priority sources, focusing specifically on updates.
To further refine control and block inserts from a specific data source, a CMDB administrator can configure IRE Data Source Rules by navigating to: Configuration > Identification/Reconciliation > IRE Data Source Rules.
When multiple data sources can update the same CI class or attributes, reconciliation rule prioritization determines which source is authoritative. This prevents authorized
sources from overwriting each other’s data and ensures a clear source of truth.
The Data Source Histories [cmdb_datasource_last_update] table in ServiceNow is used to track the last update time for each data source that contributes data to the
Configuration Management Database (CMDB). This table is populated only after reconciliation rules are configured for a specific class and data is ingested into that class.
CMDB 360 / Multisource CMDB Before the Paris release, ServiceNow CMDB could track only the last data source that updated a CI or its attributes, stored in the Data Source Histories (cmdb_datasource_last_update) table. When multiple discovery sources reported
values for the same attribute, lower-priority values were discarded by reconciliation rules, making it difficult to analyze data conflicts, compare sources, identify gaps, or improve reconciliation logic.
After the Paris release, Multisource CMDB, available through CMDB 360 in CMDB Workspace, was introduced. It retains full attribute-level history from all discovery sources—both accepted and rejected values—stored in the CMDB MultiSource Data (cmdb_multisource_data) table.
This enables CMDB administrators to track how each CI is populated, compare values across sources, revert updates from specific sources, recompute attributes after reconciliation rule changes, and better assess data quality and source coverage using CMDB 360 analytics and queries.

## CMDB 360 Query


CMDB 360 Query is a powerful feature that helps customers explore and analyze CMDB data to answer critical operational questions. It provides three main query options:
- Explore 360 Data: Understand what CI data is being reported and by which
discovery sources, enabling deep visibility into attribute-level data.
- Identify Data Mismatches: Detect inconsistencies when multiple data sources
report different values for the same CI attribute.
- Gap Analysis: Identify missing or inconsistent discovery coverage, such as when
one source reports a CI and another does not.
Using CMDB 360 Query, administrators can easily find issues like servers missing the ServiceNow Agent Client Collector or Windows servers not discovered by ServiceNow Discovery. Overall, this feature improves CMDB transparency, data quality, and confidence in discovery sources.
